title: Crossroad Eval Orchestration and Quant Compatibility Blueprint
author: Sofia Kim
content:
Overview

Purpose: This blueprint defines a pragmatic, auditable contract between the evaluation harness, prompt/catalog stewardship, model onboarding, quantization handover, and regression triage systems. It codifies the runtime and offline checks required to promote a model variant across environments (shadow -> staged -> canary -> prod) when quantized artifacts or prompt transformations are involved. The goal is to reduce surprise regressions while preserving inference cost improvements.

Scope and audience
- Scope: eval orchestration, quant handoff, prompt-set preservation, shadow-synchronization, regression fast-paths, and on-call playbooks.
- Audience: Evaluator team, Model Onboarding, Runtime, SRE, and Product Engineering.

Key outcomes
- A single set of contracts that gates model promotion when quant artifacts exist.
- Deterministic shadow synchronization semantics to ensure probes and production traffic are comparable.
- A triage ladder for regressions attributable to quantization or prompt rewrites.

Definitions
- Probe: a single eval input used by the eval harness.
- Shadow environment: runtime that mirrors production traffic for evaluation without returning responses to users.
- Quant-handoff: automated process that creates quantized model artifact, associated metadata, and signature vectors.
- Integrity contract: a JSON manifest that travels with an artifact and enumerates checks, thresholds, and lineage.

Architecture (text diagram)
- evaluator-service -> probe-orchestrator -> shadow-fleet (mirror) -> quant-handoff-service -> artifact-registry -> promotion-guard -> canary-fleet -> prod-fleet

Roles & ownership
- Evaluator team: owns probe catalog, scheduling, and evaluator-service.
- Runtime team: maintains shadow-fleet and runtime telemetry collection.
- Model onboarding: owns the promotion-guard and promotion checklists.
- Quant engineering: owns quant-handoff-service and artifact-registry metadata schema.
- SRE / oncall: owns SLA monitoring and rollback automation.

Integrity contract schema (summary table)
| field | description | example |
|---|---|---|
| artifact_id | unique artifact UUID | art-20260803-1 |
| base_model | upstream model/version | hugface/linexa-v2.1 |
| quant_profile | quantization profile id | qprofile-int8-kv-safe |
| kv_cache_compat | boolean 'true' if KV caching validated | true |
| tokenization_fingerprint | sha256 of tokenizer files | ab12..9f |
| eval_seed_set | id of probe set used for artifact certification | probe-seed-42 |
| coherence_delta | max allowed coherence drop (0-1) | 0.03 |
| latency_p50_delta_ms | allowed p50 increase vs baseline | 10 |
| rollout_tier | allowed promotion path (shadow, canary) | shadow->canary |
| owner | team or person | model-onboarding-team |

Operational contracts and thresholds
- Quality gates (artifact must pass all):
  1) Coherence (semantic agreement) delta <= 0.04 on the certified probe set.
  2) Safety sentinels: zero high-severity sentinel failures in the last 24h for the probe set.
  3) Latency: p95 increase <= 25ms vs float baseline under representative traffic.
  4) Token cost: per-token cost delta must be <= -5% (i.e., quant should reduce cost) or have a compensating business justification.
  5) Tokenization fingerprint must match onboarded tokenizer or be documented with translation mapping.

Shadow synchronization protocol (ensuring comparability)
1) Probe anchoring: Every probe executed in shadow includes a stable seed and a probe metadata header: {probe_id, probe_seed, probe_context_hash, traffic_cohort}.
2) Warmup parity: Shadow runtime executes a warmup sequence (identical priming tokens) for 3 preceding requests to stabilize KV effects.
3) Deterministic alignment: For models with nondeterministic sampling, the eval harness runs N=5 fixed-seed replicates and uses the median coherence score.
4) Telemetry alignment: Shadow telemetry must include the same routing, batching, and cache-hit labels as production for the evaluated request.

Prompt and Catalog preservation rules
- Prompt canonicalization: The prompt set associated with any promotion must be recorded using the canonicalized form and checksum. Changes to prompt wording require a labeled re-certification step.
- Prompt transformation mapping: If the runtime applies prompt truncation/compaction (e.g., context slicing), a documented mapping must be attached to the integrity contract.

Model onboarding checklist (promotion to canary)
1) Artifact integrity contract present and signed by quant-team.
2) Shadow run: 48h of shadow traffic with probes + 1% sampled production traffic mirrored.
3) Metric stability: coherence_delta <= 0.03 and deployment_sentiment score unchanged.
4) Canary plan: staging -> 5% canary traffic for 24h, with automatic rollback triggers.
5) Communication: announce to #eval-alerts and runbook-linked stakeholders 2 hours before canary start.

Rollback and regression triage ladder
- Automatic rollback triggers (applied by promotion-guard):
  - coherence drop > 0.06 on live-sampled probes in any 10-minute window.
  - safety sentinel trip (high severity) on a live probe.
  - production error rate increase > 0.5 percentage points and absolute error rate > 1.5%.
- Manual triage steps:
  1) Triage lead (oncall-evaluator) captures failing probe ids and artifact_id.
  2) Compare shadow vs prod telemetry using the alignment keys.
  3) Run focused replay: replay failing probes through float baseline + quant artifact with identical runtime labels.
  4) If regressions reproduce in replay -> escalate to quant engineering and model-owner.
  5) If regressions are absent in replay -> inspect routing, batching, and tokenizer differences; route to runtime team.
  6) Tag regression root-cause (quant|prompt|runtime|data-drift) and create an incident if severity meets thresholds.

Instrumentation and telemetry requirements (minimum)
- evaluator-service: probe_execution_time_ms, probe_seed, probe_context_hash, evaluator_version.
- shadow-fleet: p50/p95 latency, token_count, kv_cache_hit_rate, batch_size, sampling_seed_note.
- artifact-registry: artifact_id, quant_profile, fingerprint, certified_probe_set_id, certification_time.
- promotion-guard: last_promotion_run_id, checks_passed[], rollforward_deadline.

SLOs and monitoring (suggested)
- Probe-run availability: 99.9% monthly.
- Shadow telemetry freshness: < 60s lag from production events.
- Certification pipeline runtime: median 45 minutes (for small models), 6 hours (for suites > 10k probes).

Runbook snippets and CLI examples
- Create integrity contract (local sample):
  evaluator-cli create-contract --artifact art-20260803-1 --base-model hugface/linexa-v2.1 --quant-profile qprofile-int8-kv-safe --probe-set probe-seed-42 --coherence-delta 0.02

- Trigger shadow certification:
  ci/cd/pipelines/trigger-cert --artifact art-20260803-1 --env shadow --timeout 6h

- Replay a failing probe locally:
  evaluator-cli replay --probe-id probe-12034 --artifact art-20260803-1 --seed 42 --labels routing=prod,cache=on

Testing matrix (short table)
| test | purpose | owner | pass criteria |
|---|---|---|---|
| semantic-coherence-suite | semantic preservation check | evaluator | delta <= 0.03 |
| safety-sentinels | safety regression detection | quality | 0 high severity failures |
| tokenization-regression | verify tokenizer parity | model-onboarding | exact tokenization fingerprint |
| runtime-parity | ensure batching/cache parity | runtime | batch/kv labels identical |

Governance and exceptions
- Exceptions to thresholds must be recorded in the artifact's integrity contract and explicitly approved by the model-onboarding lead and a product owner.
- Emergency fast-path: If a critical cost-saving quant requires expedited rollout, a required compensating test is a 72-hour focused cohort canary with a 0.5% user exposure cap and annotated customer-impact playbook.

Appendices
- Appendix A: Example integrity contract (JSON sample) — see internal artifact-registry examples folder.
- Appendix B: Probe seeding recommendations: use fixed seeds, mark nondeterministic models, and run 5 replicates for final certification.
- Appendix C: Contact list — evaluator-team@redwood.com, runtime-oncall@redwood.com, quant-eng@redwood.com.

Related pages and references
- See: evaluation-mesh-topology-and-slotting-cookbook, quant-profile-synthesis-and-safety-playbook, shadow-orchestrator-crossmodal-stress-2026 for deeper integration patterns.
